verdict.rationale: Windmill documents workspace-level Variables and Secrets, all encrypted with a workspace-specific key. That evidences central credential storage within a shared workspace. It also has a roles and permissions system for controlling access within workspaces, but the evidence never shows that permissions can be set on individual credentials. Missing for 10: explicit per-credential sharing and access-control documentation, a dedicated resource/connection credential model, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can store connection credentials centrally, share them with my team, and control who can use which credential

citations.quote: All Variables (not just secrets) are encrypted with a workspace specific symmetric key to avoid leakage.
Windmill provides a roles and permissions system that allows you to control access and manage permissions within your instance and workspaces.
